research_notes: A safe relay should prefer losing a small amount of residual capacity over risking an incomplete final checkpoint.
The purpose of boundary search is to quantify how much reserve is actually needed rather than assume a large fixed buffer.
Start pre-arm already removes one major source of reserve demand.
Observed close overhead will determine the remaining checkpoint reserve.
Task-duration admission can then recover some otherwise abandoned tail capacity.
This is the core path from runtime measurement to a reusable handoff policy.
